title: Cal AI’s 19-year-old founder just raised $10M for his new AI startup
key_facts: Zach Yadegari, teen co-founder of calorie-tracking app Cal AI, launched Persona, an AI agent startup, and raised $10 million.
Vine Ventures led, with Z Fellows founder Cory Levy and Collective Global.
MyFitnessPal acquired Cal AI in March; Yadegari left in June.
Persona is a personal AI assistant with a $179 wearable band expected in December; it activates by button or wrist flick and is not always listening.
The model runs in Persona's cloud; data is encrypted in transit and at rest and users can delete it.
The business model currently relies on ads shown during shopping research; Yadegari says the agent does not know which items are advertised.
Persona is in free beta over iMessage with "a few thousand beta users"; the band has "five figures in preorder revenue".
quote_evidence: Zach Yadegari, the teen co-founder of calorie tracking app Cal AI, has launched Persona, a new AI agent startup, and already raised $10 million.
The bands are expected to be available in December, and an app is in the works.
Although user data won’t be sold to advertisers, the startup’s current business model does rely on ads.
why_it_matters_hint: A young founder who sold one app is entering the crowded personal AI assistant market with a wearable.
notes: Founder's own claims on privacy, ad neutrality, beta users and preorders; not independently checked.
